Roston Chase to Shreyas Iyer, SIX, maiden T20I hundred for India's T20I captain, Shreyas Iyer! Fastest by an Indian player against West Indies! This is ruthless. This is class. This is Shreyas Iyer at his very best. Tossed up by Chase, and Iyer simply hammers it over long-on for a towering six to reach the landmark. The last time he played a T20 at this venue, turning out for Punjab Kings, he smashed a hundred then too, and he has done it again tonight off just 42 deliveries, this time in India colours. He raises his bat and soaks in the applause from everyone inside the venue

Ishan Kishan (1/2): (That single to give the strike to Shreyas Iyer, easy decision for you?) Yeah, I think he was in very good touch and to be very honest, looking from the other end, I felt it's better to keep him on strike and not let the momentum stop. So my job was pretty easy in the middle, to just get off strike and let him play as many balls as he can. (In a partnership, when do you realise that you need to be the backseat driver?) I think you get to know in the middle. How the other batter is timing the ball, if I'm doing it better or he is doing it. And he looked in very good touch today. And I was not looking in such great touch, to be very honest. So I just felt it's better to keep him on strike rather than just be on strike, try those shots, but at the same time, I wanted him to keep the momentum going.

Ishan Kishan (2/2): (Talk us through that catch of yours, please) Yeah, I was not able to judge the ball because it was coming straight from the lights, but I had that slight intuition where I felt the ball's gonna appear near my waist, so I just went for it and I'm just thankful that it was in my hand afterwards. (Twenty-four hours since you guys got back together, how's the body feeling? What was the messaging around the dressing room before the start of this game?) Nothing, we just, you know, these things happen. You won't get time, sometimes you'll be put under pressure, but at the same time, looking at West Indies, how they have been playing cricket recently, our job was to, once we step on the field, once you wear the jersey, you have to give your all. Some days you won't be feeling so good, but it's our job to just give 100 percent if you're there.

Hope 2/2: [Why hold your spinners back early on?] Ideally, I would like them to be able to bowl eight overs each. We only had two of them in our side at the point in time. So we wanted to, if you got a couple more wickets, you still had a few left-handers in your back end, we could get Chase to come in and do some damage in the middle. But it just didn't work out for us today. You know, we wanted an extra spinner, but so many things you could look at in hindsight. But yeah, India played well and they played better than us today. [Are you enjoying your own form in India?] I just love batting here. So whenever I get an opportunity to come and play some cricket here, it always makes me happy.

Iyer 2/2: [Do you want to overwhelm opponents like this?] Winning definitely tastes different, and that's what we keep talking about in the dressing room. If it's your day, make sure that you win the match for the team. And today it was me. Previous couple of games, it was the batsmen who finished off the game. So yeah, overall I feel it was a comprehensive performance, and I think if we continue with the same mindset, we will be one of the destructive teams in T20s. [How impressed were you with Naman Dhir's bowling?] Yeah, special player, I must say. Like showing that attitude and approach, wanting to bowl in those crucial moments, he realized that the ball was turning, and then he capitalized on it. So commendable performance by him, and I love his attitude. [Will you get a long sleep tonight?] Looking forward to (it). I'm already sleepy. I could see Axar's eyes as well have become red. So I'm sure all of us are.

Shreyas Iyer’s tenure as India’s T20I captain began with humbling defeats in Ireland and England, but the tide has turned emphatically. Iyer and his team are now beginning to find their rhythm, with India winning each of their last 10 T20Is. And tonight, the skipper underlined his growing authority in spectacular fashion, smashing a magnificent century. West Indies will have to be far better than they were tonight if they are to beat this Indian team and fight their way back into the series. The second T20I takes place in Ranchi on Friday (October 9), and we will be here nice and early for all the action. But that’s it from us tonight. We will see you soon. Good night and take care, everyone!
